title: HOW LONG WILL YOU REFUSE TO HUMBLE YOURSELF?

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said to him, "This is what the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, says: 'How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go, so that they may worship me.'"" - Exodus 10:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's question cuts to the centre of the whole conflict: how long will you refuse to humble yourself before me?

That is what this has always been about. Not politics, not economics, not even slavery in the first instance. Pride. One man's refusal to bow.

The question is uncomfortable because it applies far beyond Pharaoh. God's requirement has never changed. He opposes the proud but shows favour to the humble (Jas 4:6). Everything in the Christian life begins with a bowed head.

Notice the phrase how long. God has been asking Pharaoh the same thing for months now. He is patient — but the question carries weight. There is a limit to how long anyone can keep saying no.

And notice that humbling is something Pharaoh must do himself: refuse to humble yourself. God does not force it. He waits.

Is there something God has been asking you for a long time, and you have kept finding reasons to delay?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What is God asking me to humble myself about?
2. How long have I been putting off something I know He has made clear?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I bow before You. Break my pride where it resists You, and help me stop delaying. Amen.
